name: SOLID + Hexagonal Architecture
description: SOLID principles with hexagonal (ports and adapters) architecture. Domain logic is isolated from infrastructure through interfaces.

rules.name: Single Responsibility
rules.instruction: Each type has exactly one reason to change. If a struct handles both business logic and I/O, split it.

rules.name: Open/Closed
rules.instruction: Extend behavior through new implementations of existing interfaces, not by modifying existing types. Use composition over inheritance.

rules.name: Liskov Substitution
rules.instruction: Any implementation of an interface must be substitutable without altering correctness. No implementation should panic on valid input or require callers to check concrete types.

rules.name: Interface Segregation
rules.instruction: Keep interfaces small and focused — one to three methods. If a consumer only needs part of an interface, define a narrower one at the point of use.

rules.name: Dependency Inversion
rules.instruction: High-level modules must not import low-level modules. Both depend on abstractions (interfaces). Domain code never imports infrastructure packages.

rules.name: Inward Dependency Rule
rules.instruction: Dependencies point inward only: adapters → application → domain. The domain layer has zero imports from outer layers. Infrastructure concerns (HTTP, database, file I/O) live in adapters.

rules.name: Ports as Interfaces
rules.instruction: Define inbound ports (interfaces the application exposes) and outbound ports (interfaces the application requires). Ports live in the domain or application layer, never in adapters.

rules.name: Adapters are Thin
rules.instruction: Adapters translate between external systems and ports. They contain no business logic — only mapping, serialization, and protocol handling.

rules.name: Constructor Injection
rules.instruction: Pass dependencies through constructors, not global state or service locators. Every dependency is explicit in the function signature.

rules.name: No Domain Leakage
rules.instruction: Domain types must not leak infrastructure concerns: no JSON tags on domain entities, no ORM annotations, no framework-specific types in domain signatures.

rules.name: Errors as Values
rules.instruction: Return errors explicitly. Never panic for recoverable conditions. Every error must be handled — logged or propagated — never silently ignored.
